A.explanation: These values are half the correct voltages and would correspond to using $V_2$ as the voltage of the whole lower branch instead of one resistor.

B.explanation: The lower branch p.d. is $2 \times 1.0 = 2.0 \text{ V}$, so $V_4 = 2.0 \text{ V}$, and the series current is 3 times the lower-branch current, so $V_3 = 3.0 \text{ V}$.

C.explanation: These values overestimate the voltages and do not satisfy $V = IR$ with identical $R$ for the 1-resistor and 2-resistor parallel branches.

D.explanation: These values would make $V_3 +$ parallel p.d. exceed $V_1 = 8.0 \text{ V}$ when the left vertical resistor is included.

hints: Notice $V_2 = 1.0 \text{ V}$ is across only the right-hand resistor of the lower branch, which has two identical resistors in series.
Remember the upper single-resistor branch is in parallel with that two-resistor lower branch, so both branches share the same p.d. and $V = IR$ controls the current split.
Compare the total current returning to the battery with the current in the $V_2$ resistor, then apply $V = IR$ to the single series resistor measured by $V_3$.
walkthrough: Identify the series loop: the $8.0 \text{ V}$ measured by $V_1$ drives current through the left vertical resistor, then the $V_3$ resistor, then the right parallel combination back to the battery.
Analyse the lower right branch: it is two identical resistors of resistance $R$ in series. Let its current be $I$. Then $V_2 = IR = 1.0 \text{ V}$.

Find the p.d. of the whole right parallel combination. The lower branch p.d. is $I \times 2R = 2IR = 2.0 \text{ V}$. The upper branch is in parallel with it, so $V_4$ equals this value, $2.0 \text{ V}$.
Find the total current. Upper branch current is $2.0/R = 2I$, lower branch current is $I$, so total current leaving the junction is $3I$. This $3I$ flows through the $V_3$ series resistor.

Calculate $V_3 = 3I \times R = 3IR = 3 \times 1.0 = 3.0 \text{ V}$. Check: $3.0 + 2.0 = 5.0 \text{ V}$ leaves $3.0 \text{ V}$ for the remaining left resistor, totalling $8.0 \text{ V}$. This is option B.
